Command: The breastplate shall not be loosened from the ephod
Summary: The command: The breastplate shall not be loosened from the ephod (Exodus 28:28). The breastplate of judgment was bound to the ephod with blue lace so it would not come loose during service.
Commandment: The breastplate shall not be loosened from the ephod.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches the earthly tabernacle was a copy of the heavenly one, and Christ now serves as high priest in the true tabernacle.
Purpose: To give Israel a mediated approach to God through the tabernacle pattern (Exodus 25:40). Hebrews teaches the earthly copy gave way to Christ's priesthood in the true tabernacle (Hebrews 8:1-6).
Function: The breastplate of judgment was bound to the ephod with blue lace so it would not come loose in service — a small, exact detail, and that exactness is what makes this ceremonial. Its goal was to keep the stones bearing the tribes' names fixed over Aaron's heart whenever he ministered. Scripture gives no particular evil this restrained, and I will not invent one; its work was order and remembrance, not restraint. The breastplate stayed put, so the people stayed on the priest's heart.
